content.text:
I fixed the crash: `Papa.unparse([[null], ['hello']], { skipEmptyLines: true })` now outputs `hello` instead of throwing, and a single-cell row containing `undefined` is skipped the same way. The full test suite has one failure, in a test unrelated to this change (details below).

**Cause:** the empty-line check in `serialize` at `papaparse.js:336` read the cell's `.length` directly (`data[row][0].length === 0`). It only runs when `skipEmptyLines` is `true`, which is why `false` and `'greedy'` worked. A `null` or `undefined` cell has no `.length`, so it crashed.

**Fix:** the check now also counts `null` and `undefined` as empty, which matches how they're already exported (as empty cells). Every other value is checked as before.

**Test:** I added a case to `tests/test-cases.js`: `[[null], ['hello'], [undefined], ['world']]` with `skipEmptyLines: true` should give `hello\r\nworld`.

**Results:** 255 passing, 25 pending, 1 failing. The failure is "Pause and resume works (Regression Test for Bug #636)" in `tests/node-tests.js`, which hits its 30-second timeout, including when run on its own. It tests pausing and resuming while parsing, and never calls `unparse`, so my change can't reach it. I couldn't confirm it also fails without my change: when I tried to set my changes aside with `git stash` to check, the command needed approval and didn't run. Your working tree is unchanged.
